AI Stock Correction? 3 SGX Stocks Worth Another Look
article:
Once a niche tech theme, artificial intelligence (AI) is now a defining global investment trend as tech giants and sovereign nations race to massively expand computing power, data centre footprints, and chip manufacturing capacity.
But recent market volatility forced many AI supply-chain-related companies to undergo brutal recalibrations in valuation multiples.
Not every such company will benefit equally from the
AI theme
. Still, for quality enablers – those with competitive moats, pricing power, recurring revenues, and balance sheet resilience – market volatility simply means greater upside opportunities for fundamental-focused investors.
These three SGX-listed stocks could make the cut as such quality enablers.
Keppel DC REIT (SGX: AJBU): Powering High-Density AI Workloads
The exponential growth of AI workloads into the megawatt (MW)-per-rack scale calls for a complete overhaul of traditional data centres (DC), which were typically designed to handle only kilowatt (kW)-scale racks, benefiting
Keppel DC REIT
.
Keppel DC REIT is a key player in this fundamental shift of data centre infrastructure.
In the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), the REIT’s gross revenue surged 13.3% year on year (YoY) to S$365.3 million, driving net property income up comparably by 13.1% to S$316.8 million.
Positive rental reversions and escalations, alongside accretive acquisitions, contributed to the strong operating performance.
All told, Keppel DC REIT’s 9M2026 distribution per unit (DPU) was raised by 11.7% YoY to S$0.08571 – that’s an annualised distribution yield of 5.2% at a unit price of S$2.20.
As Asia’s first pure-play data centre REIT, Keppel DC REIT has S$7.6 billion in assets under management (AUM), spanning 27 DCs across 10 countries, with a 93.4% occupancy rate and a long 6.6-year weighted average lease expiry (WALE).
With a leverage ratio of 36.2% and an average debt cost of 2.6% for 9M2026, the REIT’s distributions are backed by a strong balance sheet.
With the recently-completed S$1.37 billion acquisitions of Tokyo Data Centres 4 and 5 generating immediate 2.0% DPU accretion, Keppel DC REIT’s growth remains unabated.
UMS Integration Limited (SGX: 558): Unmatched Precision Tooling for Front-End Semiconductor Giants
Global semiconductor equipment sales are projected to reach US$229.5 billion in 2028, benefiting precision-engineering semiconductor partners such as UMS.
Long known for its high-profile partnership with
Applied Materials
(NASDAQ: AMAT), UMS has onboarded a second major global semiconductor equipment customer, believed to be Lam Research. This transforms UMS into a dual-engine growth story.
In the first half of 2026 (1H2026), UMS’s revenue rose 25% YoY to S$156.5 million, while net profit surged 66% to S$33.4 million, powered by its high 54.2% gross material margin in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q2026).
Amid renewed interest rate hikes, UMS recently raised S$140.8 million via a private placement to fund its factory expansion in Penang, rather than taking on more debt.
This prudent financing allows the company to operate with a net cash position of S$29.3 million and no interest-bearing bank borrowings as of 30 June 2026.
For investors, UMS is a targeted bet on globally rising chip equipment spending.
AEM Holdings Ltd (SGX: AWX): High-Power Thermal Control and System-Level Testing for Next-Generation AI Chips
As semiconductor architectures shift to nodes of 3nm and lower, testing AI chiplets is becoming exponentially more complex than before.
This complexity calls for a robust System-Level Testing (SLT) solution to detect potential failures due to thermal stress.
AEM addresses this with its high-parallel SLT systems, which feature a proprietary PiXL dynamic thermal regulation engine, and achieve precise, reliable, active thermal control.
AEM’s 1H2026 revenue was up 29.9% YoY to S$247.2 million, while net profit jumped 875.6% to S$30.8 million, driven by top-line growth of 52.5% from its Test Cell Solutions segment.
With an order backlog that exceeded S$400 million for its AMPS platform, management remains optimistic about
AEM’s growth momentum
, having upgraded its FY2026 revenue guidance to a range of S$630 million to S$680 million from S$550 million to S$600 million previously.
Furthermore, AEM’s partnership with
ASE Technology Holding Co. Ltd
(NYSE: ASX) – the world’s largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider – enables AEM to deliver its disruptive test solutions for the rising AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC) markets through ASE’s world-class manufacturing scale.
As investors are increasingly concerned with US tech titans’ mounting leverage, AEM sets itself apart with a strong balance sheet, supported by S$56.6 million in net cash and a low 0.05x debt-to-equity ratio.
Get Smart: Navigating the AI Cycle with Fundamental Strength
Market corrections provide investors with an opportunity to discern whether the pullbacks are justified by declining fundamentals or simply driven by short-term sentiment.
While Singapore may not have homegrown AI chip designers, the tiny city-state holds its own with companies that play key supporting roles for US-based, mover-and-shaker AI enablers.
Keppel DC’s income is defensible as high-density compute continues to be in short supply.
While UMS captures the expanding front-end equipment spending, AEM benefits as thermal testing becomes almost non-negotiable for mission-critical chip deployments.
Both UMS and AEM also operate with an enviable net cash position and low debt.

title: Gold extends fall below US$4,000 as market watches Fed
article:
(Nov 12): Gold fell for a third day, extending its decline below US$4,000 an ounce after persistent US inflation and hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve officials reinforced expectations for a series of interest-rate hikes.

Bullion fell as much as 1.6%, taking losses over the past three sessions to about 5% at one point. Traders are fully pricing in a quarter-point increase in December, while some even see a chance of a half-point hike. Higher borrowing costs are typically a drag on gold as it doesn’t pay interest.

Gold has struggled to sustain its brief rebound above US$4,100 an ounce late last month, which came as oil prices fell and equity markets staged a cautious recovery.

Yields on two-year Treasuries, which are sensitive to near-term rate policy, have surged around 20 basis points so far this week, while a gauge of the dollar jumped almost 1% in the previous two sessions before steadying on Thursday.

The precious metal faces further downside risk amid a less favourable macro environment, potentially falling towards US$3,870 an ounce, Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, said in a note. Any upside surprise to the US producer price index due on Friday “risks extending the recent pullback” in precious metals, he added.

See also: Singapore extends GST waiver to activities related to wholesale gold transactions

Traders will be monitoring commentary by US Federal Reserve governor Michael S Barr and other central bank officials on Thursday. A day earlier, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago president Austan Goolsbee said October’s hotter-than-expected consumer inflation report was “borderline disturbing.”

Spot gold was down 1% at US$3,947.69 an ounce as of 11.17am in London, while silver fell 1% to US$51.10. Platinum and palladium also edged lower. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was steady.

title: Bitcoin retreats as Nvidia turmoil weighs on risk appetite
article:
(Nov 12): Bitcoin retreated on Thursday as renewed unease over technology stocks weighed on risk appetite, with persistent withdrawals from US spot exchange-traded funds adding to the pressure.

The original cryptocurrency fell as much as 1.6% and was trading around US$73,500 as of early morning in New York. Other cryptocurrencies also weakened along with US stock futures, which were dragged lower as concerns over leadership turmoil at Nvidia Corp weighed on the artificial intelligence trade.

The chipmaker’s shares slumped as much as 10% in late US trading on Wednesday. Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for chief executive officer Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China, Bloomberg News reported.

Bitcoin’s recovery from its 2026 low below US$58,000 in July has recently faltered. It touched a three-month low on Wednesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation increased expectations for further interest-rate hikes.

“Bitcoin is showing signs of a changing market structure, with selling pressure concentrated in derivatives while spot market activity remains comparatively resilient,” Dean Chen, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitunix, said in a note on Thursday.

Futures cumulative volume delta — a measure that tracks whether buyers or sellers are more aggressive in the futures market over time — has turned deeply negative, while open interest also declined. “Taken together, these indicators suggest that leveraged exposure is cooling, but market positioning remains mixed,” Chen said.

See also: Double-clicking on crypto exchange safeguards

Other headwinds have also been building. Democrats scored a sweeping victory in the US elections last week, handing them control of both chambers of Congress next year. That will put the legislative branch at odds with President Donald Trump’s more crypto-friendly Republican administration. Democrats made Trump’s growing crypto fortune an issue in midterm campaigns.

Flows into spot Bitcoin ETFs reversed on Oct 30, four days before the election. Since then, the funds have seen roughly US$2.5 billion in net outflows.

MSCI Inc’s decision to drop Strategy Inc, the largest corporate buyer of Bitcoin, from its global equity benchmarks has been another factor affecting the cryptocurrency, according to Caroline Mauron, co-founder of Orbit Markets.

See also: Coinbase gets final regulatory stamp for trust-bank charter

“While that decision was widely expected, it added to the febrile mood around the asset class since the midterms,” she said, referring to elections in the US. “In the short term, there is a lack of support to the downside, with the next key level to watch at US$70,000.”

title: Merck KGaA lifts outlook again on life science strength
article:
(Nov 12): Merck KGaA raised its outlook for a third time, helped by the strength of its lab-equipment division and a better-than-expected performance of its multiple sclerosis drug, which is facing generic competition.

Full-year adjusted earnings are now expected to reach as much as €6.4 billion, up from the previous upper-end forecast of €6.3 billion, the company said on Thursday. It also increased its net sales guidance for the year.

The German science group said favourable foreign-exchange effects, a strong third quarter, and its soon-to-be-completed acquisition of Bio-Techne Corp, Merck’s largest deal in more than a decade, drove its upgrade.

After multiple failed efforts to stave off patent challenges to its blockbuster MS drug Mavenclad, Merck said it now expects no sales at all in the US from November. However, this is slightly better than previous guidance that US Mavenclad sales growth would stop in August.

Shares rose as much as 3.1% on Thursday in early Frankfurt trading, reaching the highest intraday price since October 2024. The stock is up about 24% this year through Wednesday’s close.

Chief executive officer Kai Beckmann is seeking to improve performance across Merck’s three businesses: healthcare, life science and electronics. Since he took the top job in May, Beckmann has already carried out two major acquisitions to bolster its pipeline, including the US$11.3 billion purchase of life-sciences company Bio-Techne, which should complete in December, and UK biotech Silence Therapeutics plc.

See also: EU targets social media addiction and online ‘dark patterns’

Acquisitions will continue to be “an important element of our strategy” going forward, Beckmann said on a media call, adding that the focus is on technology and innovation rather than simply growth.

Merck is also pursuing workforce reductions as part of a “strategic realignment” of the businesses. Asked about the size of the reductions, chief financial officer Helene von Roeder said they aren’t on the scale recently seen in other industries, declining to be more specific.

Merck’s “healthy showing” in the life science business and a “standout” performance in the electronics unit, helped it beat expectations in the third quarter, according to Alphavalue’s analyst Abhishek Raval.

See also: Spain’s main unions hold nationwide strike over housing costs

Life sciences, Merck’s biggest division, grew in the latest quarter, boosted by process solutions, which supplies drug-making equipment. The business had previously benefitted from increased demand from customers in Asia-Pacific due to worries over supply chain disruptions related to the Middle East crisis, though the company said current customer order trends point to a softer fourth quarter.

In its healthcare unit, organic sales edged higher during the third quarter as Merck’s new rare-disease therapies helped offset stiffer competition for cancer drug Bavencio and Mavenclad. Sales of the latter declined about 25%.

Electronics, the smallest unit, posted about 13% organic sales growth. Its semiconductor solutions business grew almost 19% organically, accelerating from the previous quarter on demand for materials used in artificial intelligence (AI)-related chip production.

Asked about a slowdown in data center construction after the US midterm elections, Beckmann said AI growth extends beyond just that build out. “There’s a lot still to happen in AI,” he said, pointing to industrial and edge AI, where applications run in factories, machines and devices. “We’re not yet scratching the surface.”

The German company is unrelated to Merck & Co in the US. The two drugmakers share historical roots but have been separate since World War I.

title: BP in talks to sell stake in Brazil oil discovery to Petrobras — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): BP Plc is in talks with Petrobras to sell a stake in the Bumerangue oil block off the coast of Brazil, its biggest discovery in 25 years, according to people familiar with the matter.

Negotiations between the two oil firms are ongoing and it’s possible a deal may not materialise, according to the people, who asked not to be identified because the talks are not public.

BP declined to comment on the matter. Petroleo Brasileiro SA, as Brazil’s state-controlled company is formally known, didn’t reply to requests for comment.

Petrobras has expertise in deepwater operations and has also been developing technology to separate CO2-rich gas from oil more efficiently and at a lower cost. That could address Bumerangue’s challenges as early samples from the reservoir, located in Brazil’s Santos basin, showed high levels of carbon dioxide, which could make development complicated.

BP has said the discovery has approximately eight billion barrels of liquids in place. The company will be gathering data from an appraisal drilling campaign in the coming months conducted by Halliburton Co, according to chief executive officer Meg O’Neill. A final investment decision is not expected before 2027, she has said.

“The engineering team is working on two paths,” O’Neill said in late October on an earnings conference call. “One is looking at early production systems and what sort of opportunity might present itself to accelerate revenue from this discovery, as well as then the full field development.”

See also: Rising fuel flows through Hormuz may help ease strained market

BP notified Brazilian regulators last month of a hydrocarbon discovery in the adjacent Tupinamba block of the Santos Basin, where BP operates with a 50% working interest alongside Shell Plc. Once BP completes drilling that section of Tupinamba, O’Neill said “we will be able to move over to Bumerangue.”

Focusing on BP’s strongest upstream assets is something shareholders expect from BP’s new top boss O’Neill, the company’s first outsider CEO. The UK oil major seeks to replenish oil reserves and increase production, turning around years of underperformance. Bumerangue is an important piece of the pipeline that offers long-term promise.

Petrobras has increasingly searched for new exploration opportunities, targeting offshore basins in Brazil and overseas areas where it can apply decades of expertise in deepwater drilling and production. The company recently announced oil finds in a controversial exploration area off the coast of the Amazon rainforest.

See also: Oil extends drop as Trump says further Iran strikes unnecessary

CEO Magda Chambriard said in September that Petrobras will need to add about nine billion barrels of oil equivalent to its reserves through 2050 to maintain production levels. Output from the prolific pre-salt is expected to peak around the middle of the next decade.

title: Genting Singapore 3QFY2026 earnings down 42% y-o-y on weaker gaming revenue
article:
Genting Singapore has reported earnings of $54.7 million for its 3QFY2026, down 42% y-o-y. Revenue in the same three months ended Sept was down 13% to $566.1 million, with its key gaming revenue portion down by more than a fifth to $315 million.

The integrated resort operator blames "softer premium gaming activity", and points out that this is a trend seen across regional key markets.

On the other hand, non-gaming revenue held steady despite smaller number of hotel room nights available.

The company says that due to ongoing upgrading of its facilities, the temporary constrain on its operating capacity will stretch through this coming FY2027.

"The group is focused on capturing year-end travel and festive demand as RWS enters the final quarter of 2026.

"Alongside these near-term priorities, the group continues to advance its resort-wide renewal, reinforcing Resort World Sentosa’s position as an integrated destination and laying the foundation for long-term growth and competitiveness," says Genting Singapore, whose share price closed at 61 cents on Nov 12, down 0.81% for the day, extending a drop of 16.44% year to date.

title: HSBC plans SRTs tied to US$7 bil of US, Asian corporate loans — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): HSBC Holdings Plc is working on two significant risk transfer deals to hedge around US$7 billion ($9 billion) of large corporate loans in the US and Asia.

The London-based lender is looking to take advantage of investor appetite for the loss-absorbing instruments with a transaction tied to about US$3 billion of US loans, according to people familiar with the matter.

It is also discussing a deal linked to about A$5.8 billion of lending in the Asia-Pacific region, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

SRTs typically insure a first loss or junior tranche of a loan book, generally equivalent to between 5% and 15% of the portfolio value. Issuance has boomed in recent years, enabling mainly European and North American lenders to offload risk tied to US$1 trillion in loans and to release regulatory capital for new lending, shareholder payouts or acquisitions.

Banks are selling SRTs at a record pace this year despite recent signs that investors are demanding better terms in the face of robust supply and wider credit market volatility. Sales are on track to reach about US$45 billion, with deals hedging AI-related assets seeing particularly strong growth, according to Crescent Capital Group LP, which invests in the securities.

HSBC has overhauled its business following the appointment of CEO Georges Elhedery in September 2024, shuttering, selling or merging several business lines and cutting thousands of jobs as it looks to refocus on its core Asian markets. It is also becoming more reliant on Hong Kong after announcing a US$14 billion takeover of partly-owned Hang Seng Bank Ltd last year.

See also: Bosch to separate auto-parts unit as Chinese rivals gain ground

Other banks are adding to the SRT pipeline. Spain’s BBVA SA is finalising a deal tied to about €4 billion of loans to mid-size corporates from its Vela SRT programme, according to people familiar with the matter. It is pricing at about 725 basis points over a borrowing benchmark, the people said, asking not to be identified because the deal is private.

ING Groep NV is also on track to complete a transaction tied to €4 billion of loans to small and mid-size companies originated by its unit in Belgium, other people familiar with the matter said. The SRT will hedge a junior piece of the portfolio, equivalent to about 5% of its value.

See also: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs in AI-fuelled push to lower costs

Representatives for BBVA and Amsterdam-based ING declined to comment.

title: Alibaba shares drop 7% as Nvidia saga triggers chip access fears
article:
(Nov 12): Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) stocks tumbled on concerns that cloud operators’ access to advanced chips may face tighter US scrutiny amid the escalating espionage and leadership controversy surrounding Nvidia Corp.

Alibaba Group Holding Ltd slumped as much as 7.3%, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index lower. The Internet giant rents Nvidia chips through Singapore-based Megaspeed International, whose founder had an affair with Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang and is suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Peers across the AI ecosystem also fell, with model developers Z.AI Co and MiniMax Group Inc sliding at least 8% each.

Chinese hyperscalers face a new geopolitical overhang just as investors are taking profits ahead of next week’s earnings season, when Alibaba and Tencent Holdings Ltd are due to report September-quarter results. Access to advanced chips has been crucial for Chinese AI model developers, which have been competing with US firms for market share in coding and agentic workflows.

“Now that scrutiny is ramping up, how long that tighter enforcement lasts will pose a real challenge for Chinese cloud service providers,” said Julia Pan, an analyst for UOB Kay Hian. “They’ve been stockpiling chips since the start of the year, so they have some buffer, but R&D timelines will inevitably be postponed.”

Nvidia has spent years lobbying Washington to allow it to sell more chips to Chinese customers. Those efforts are now coming under intense scrutiny because of the allegations surrounding Megaspeed founder Alice Huang and her relationship with Nvidia’s CEO.

See also: Tencent founder rallies half of staff behind AI-native push

While Chinese chipmakers have fast caught up in their capabilities, supply remains constrained and the likes of Alibaba continue to seek Nvidia’s advanced chips to support AI and keep their vast cloud infrastructure running.

“China’s sizable grey market for restricted Nvidia GPUs has long been an open secret and a glaring loophole in US export controls,” said Chai Chaoyi, a researcher at 86Research. “A high-profile crackdown could deter major intermediaries and materially disrupt this supply.”

Beijing on Thursday urged the US not to use allegations of Chinese spying on Nvidia’s Huang to justify technology restrictions, adding that the two sides remained in contact ahead of a planned meeting between their leaders.
